releaseNotes: Third PR review round: check-motion-contract.ts's two newest R12 checks (3c's inline spring-family restatement, 3d's offset table) each had a required-match gap. 3c's familyInlineRe loop had no zero-match assertion, so removing or rewording R12's press-family restatement would silently stop validating all four spring bounds. 3d only verified that a recomputed worst-case total string appeared somewhere in the file rather than parsing each table row -- a false pass was live: 2 assets' worst case (580ms) was never actually checked, because the validator's un-capped computation produced 600ms, which coincidentally already appears elsewhere in the file (the window statement). Rewrote 3d as a real per-row table parser: locates the Assets/Offset/Worst-case-total table by header, parses each row's own asset count/offset/total together, and asserts each row is internally consistent (offset x gaps + settle = total) against the current tokens, not just present somewhere in the prose. Also verifies the terminal "N+" row names the correct first-unachievable asset count.

Generalized the welcome-screen prompt library from Appllama's top-welcome-screens (github.com/Appllama/top-welcome-screens) into the skill as motion-craft-benchmarks.md's R11-R14: splash hold-and-cut, staggered multi-asset entrance, honest loader state-switch/skeleton reveal, and paged cold-open with a deterministic final state. Followed the file's existing 60fps.design pattern exactly — numeric, checkable recipes bound to the token scale, never a named app's mascot/wordmark/copy — so the source repo's own NOTICE.md licensing requirement and this file's recipe format agree by construction.

Cross-linked onboarding-conversion.md with a new Cold-Launch / Splash Entrance subsection under Conversion Patterns, pointing to the R11-R14 recipes before the screen-by-screen sequence table starts. Registered github-appllama-top-welcome-screens in source-registry.yaml (inspiration_benchmark) and widened the motion-craft-benchmarks.md and onboarding-conversion.md reference loadWhen triggers plus domain.experience's routeWhen to name welcome/splash screens explicitly, so the capability is discoverable from SKILL.md's Domain Routing table, not just reachable by an agent that already knew to look.

PR review (Codex) caught seven real gaps in R11-R14 before merge, all fixed. R11: Reduce Motion was skipping the real loading gate, not just the authored transition, and hid a stalled load's status from assistive technology entirely -- both now split decorative branding (hidden from the a11y tree) from a real loading state (exposed, noninteractive). R12: the 120-180ms stagger offset had no asset-count cap, so 4+ assets could blow the 600ms durationReveal budget -- now capped at 3 assets at the reference offset with a derivation formula for more; separately, its stated window used seconds (0.3-0.6s) that admitted a 300-359ms band durationSlow's actual 360ms token value forbids -- restated in ms to match the token exactly. R14: Reduce Motion jumped a multi-page cold-open straight to its final state, silently dropping page content the user never chose to skip -- it now replays every page with cuts instead of slides, reserving the final-state jump for an explicit skip-intro control. Workspace template: product/ONBOARDING.md had no Cold Launch row, so onboarding-conversion.md's own instruction to record the R11-R14 recipe there was unfulfillable -- added. Validator: check-motion-contract.ts never parsed R11-R14's own numeric claims, so a future token edit could silently invert R12's window while the gate stayed green -- added a new recipe-window mirror check (motion_contract.recipe_window.value_drift) plus a fail-then-catch fixture that seeds exactly that drift.

Two downstream gates caught by CI after the review-fix commit landed. check:analytics-catalog: the new Cold Launch row names cold_launch_viewed, but analytics/ANALYTICS.md's Event Contract table didn't carry the row yet -- added (fires when a paged cold-open with real page content mounts, per R14). check:generated-pages: product/onboarding.html was stale relative to the edited ONBOARDING.md -- re-rendered via render-artifact-pages.ts --root workspace/business (the default --root resolves to a nonexistent top-level business/ dir, not workspace/business/).

A second PR review round caught the prior fix's own math error plus a validator gap in the fix itself. R12: the 'capped at 3 assets at the full reference offset' claim was wrong -- worst case, 2 gaps at 180ms plus a 400ms settle totals 760ms, still over the 600ms cap. Redid the arithmetic from the worst-case settle (press family's slowest 0.4s response) down: 200ms of gap budget remains, so 2 assets safely use the full 120-180ms reference range (580ms worst case), 3 assets must shrink to <=100ms (600ms exactly), 4 assets to <=66ms (598ms, still above the 60ms stagger floor), and 5+ assets cannot satisfy both the 600ms window and the 60ms floor at once -- the table states this explicitly instead of a formula that quietly breaks past 4. Validator: check-motion-contract.ts's new recipe-window check parsed each match's values but never asserted a match existed at all, so rewording the parenthetical away would make it silently validate nothing -- added motion_contract.recipe_window.none_found plus a fixture. Also added motion_contract.recipe_family_inline.drift to catch a recipe's own inline spring-family restatement (R12's 'press-family spring (response 0.3-0.4s, damping 0.7-0.8)') drifting from premium-mobile-craft.md's table, the same drift class the existing family-mirror check already covered for the file's one summary sentence but not for an individual recipe body.
